home.lede: The open archive of the world's sports results. It is not a live-results site: it is a newspaper archive. Every closed edition is published with its date, its matchday and the provenance of each datum.
home.what.title: What it is (and what it is not)
home.what.is.1: A historical archive: only closed editions, with their date and matchday.
home.what.is.2: Open data under the Creative Commons BY 4.0 licence.
home.what.is.4: Multilingual: Spanish, English, Portuguese, Chinese and Hindi.
home.what.is.5: With cited sources: every datum points to its origin.
home.build.title: How it is built
home.build.step1.text: Every edition starts from identified external sources, consulted with a date.
home.build.step2.text: It records which source each datum comes from and what was discarded.
home.build.step3.text: Schema, languages, countries, sources and consistency are checked on every change.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.lede: How Proyecto Libero collects, records and publishes its results.
methodology.sources.title: Where the data comes from
methodology.sources.text: Every datum comes from identified external sources consulted with a date. We do not publish results without a source: each edition declares its sources and retrieval date.
methodology.provenance.title: Provenance
methodology.provenance.text: Every datum records which source it comes from, with the primary source marked with a star, and which alternatives were discarded and why. Provenance is auditable edition by edition.
methodology.validation.title: Validation
methodology.validation.text: Before publication the project goes through automatic checks: data schema, parity across the five languages, country codes, cited sources and consistency between index and edition. If any fails, publication is blocked.
methodology.coverage.title: Coverage
methodology.coverage.text: Every edition declares its coverage: complete, partial or absent. "Partial" means the source does not offer all the data; "absent", that it is not available yet.
methodology.phases.title: Declared phases and completion
methodology.phases.text: An edition is considered complete when it has all the phases declared by the catalogue published, plus its champion. Absent or partial phases are shown explicitly.
methodology.cite.title: How to cite
methodology.cite.text: You may cite Proyecto Libero by stating the release version and the retrieval date. The data is distributed under the CC BY 4.0 licence.
license.title: License and use
license.lede: What you may do with Proyecto Libero's code and data.
license.code.title: Code
license.code.text: The project's code is published under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0).
license.data.title: Data
license.data.text: The data and its compilation (catalogue, data and releases) are distributed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0).
license.verbatim.title: Verbatim sheets
license.verbatim.text: Match sheets reproduce the cited sources literally and are included with their attribution; they are not relicensed. Their rights belong to their original authors.
license.rights.title: What you may and may not do
license.rights.can.1: Use the data for any purpose.
license.rights.can.3: Adapt it and combine it with other data.
license.rights.can.4: Cite the source as required by the licence.
license.rights.cannot.1: Remove the attribution to Proyecto Libero or to the original sources.
license.download.title: Download
license.download.text: The JSON of each edition is served at /data/… and the site's general index at /index.json.
license.never.title: We never sell data
license.never.text: The information is free and open. We do not sell data to companies; the project is sustained by donations and collaborating institutions.
contribute.title: How to contribute
contribute.lede: Proyecto Libero is built with the community.
contribute.offer.title: What you can contribute
contribute.offer.1: Data: missing results or unpublished editions.
contribute.offer.2: Corrections: errors in results, dates or names.
contribute.offer.4: Code: improvements to the generator, the validator or the design.
contribute.propose.title: How to propose it
contribute.propose.text: Open an issue or a pull request in the repository. Every data contribution must cite its source, with URL and retrieval date.
contribute.after.title: What happens next
contribute.after.text: The proposal goes through automatic validation, a human review and, if everything is correct, publication. Every contribution is recorded with its author, date and source.
contribute.trust.title: Confidence levels
contribute.trust.text: Provenance distinguishes primary, cross-checked and discarded sources; a datum is only published when its confidence level is justified.
contribute.links.title: Links
contribute.links.text: See the repository's contribution guides: CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/CONTRIBUCION.md.
contribute.flow.note: Every contribution keeps its author, its date and its source.
contribute.form.title: Contribution form
contribute.form.lede: Fill in the form and, if your browser runs JavaScript, GitHub will open with the issue pre-filled. If not, use the direct link to the template, which always works.
contribute.form.confirm: I confirm that the source is citable and that I can share this information.
contribute.form.invalid: Fill in the description, the source and the confirmation before continuing.
contribute.form.nojs: You can also contribute without JavaScript:
contribute.form.nojs.link: Open the contribution template on GitHub
contribute.form.option.a: Template (recommended): asks for the fields one by one and always works, with or without JavaScript.
contribute.form.option.b: Blank issue: GitHub ignores the body in templates, so this route uses the blank page; the text is only pre-filled with JavaScript.
support.title: Support the project
support.lede: The archive is free and open; keeping it so has a cost. This page explains what a donation pays for and what it does not buy.
support.why.title: Why
support.why.text: Proyecto Libero is free information: the data is not sold and nobody pays to consult it. Keeping it accessible and correcting an error whenever one shows up takes time and money. Donations cover that part, without changing anyone's access.
support.costs.title: What it pays for
support.costs.1: Infrastructure: Cloudflare and GitHub, where the archive is hosted and versioned.
support.costs.2: Artificial intelligence: the models that help build and maintain the archive.
support.costs.3: Services needed to scale to more sports and competitions.
support.costs.4: Repaying part of the hundreds of hours of work already invested.
support.notbuy.title: What a donation does not buy
support.notbuy.1: It does not buy the data: it stays free and open.
support.notbuy.2: It gives no privileged or early access.
support.notbuy.3: It does not change the content or its truthfulness: no one can alter a result by paying.
support.transparency.title: Transparency
support.transparency.text: Every year a report is published with what was received and how it was spent. The methodology and the sustainability document explain the detail.
support.status.title: Who is behind it
support.status.text: Proyecto Libero is maintained by an individual: it is not an NGO or a foundation. Donations are handled as such, with the tax treatment of a natural person.
support.institution.text: If you represent a university, an archive or a library, a separate path for collaborating entities exists.
support.action.title: Donations
support.action.text: Sponsorship is handled through GitHub Sponsors.
support.donate.label: Sponsor on GitHub
support.donate.note: Opens GitHub Sponsors in a new tab.
support.pending: Path in preparation. The donation link will be published here as soon as it is available.
